title: Cover callbacks in S7 shared class definitions
description:
Coverage of installed S7 classes currently reports zero for property getters, setters, and validators with development S7. Installed constructors can be byte-compiled copies of the definition used by instances.

Traverse the shared class definition when gathering callback replacements, so instrumentation reaches the closures that instance access calls. Classes without the shared reference retain the existing traversal.

title: fix bug in src/reassign.c
description:
Credit here, like it or not, to Claude for uncovering this one. I used to also use `SET_BODY` in [one package of mine](https://github.com/mpadge/typetracer). When R removed export of the `SET_` functions from `Rinternals.h`, I looked here for how you got around it, and ended up wholesale copying your approach - with full attribution!

I encountered an odd bug in my code, and set Claude on a debugging session. It came up with this solution, which indeed works. This is an edited version of the Claude comment:

---

The struct copy in the C code  wires 'new's formals/body/env directly into 'old_fun' without going through R's normal SET_FORMALS/SET_BODY/ SET_CLOENV setters. Those setters exist not just to assign the pointer, but also to run the generational-GC write barrier (so that an old-generation object such as 'old_fun', which may already have survived several collections, is flagged as now referencing potentially younger objects). Skipping that barrier is safe as long as the referenced objects can never be reclaimed while 'old_fun' still points to them. 'R_PreserveObject' is the public, API-stable way to guarantee that: it keeps an object alive for the remainder of the session regardless of the normal generational reachability scan. That permanently retains these (typically small) formals/body/env objects, which is an acceptable trade-off for a tracing tool to avoid the alternative: a GC collecting them out from under 'old_fun' the next time a minor collection runs, corrupting the traced function.

title: Keep parse text only for terminal tokens
description:
`get_parse_data()` calls `getParseData(includeText = TRUE)`, which extracts the source text of every expression. covr only reads the text of terminal tokens (the `...` check for switch arms), and `includeText = NA` still provides that.

Tracing a package with about 29,000 traces gives identical counters, srcrefs and traced functions, and takes about 10 s instead of 20 s. Every process that loads the instrumented package pays this, including each parallel testthat worker.

title: Look up shared traces by index in merge_coverage()
description:
`merge_coverage.list()` indexes the coverage list by name inside its loop, which is a linear search per trace, so merging grows quadratically with the number of traces.

This matches the shared names once and indexes by position. The merged result is identical.

On a package with about 29,000 traces, merging the five trace files of a parallel test run (the main process and four testthat workers) went from 61 s to 0.7 s.

title: Fix compiled test fixture for R 4.6
description:
## Cause

The recent release/devel CI jobs fail while installing `TestCompiled`. R 4.6 no longer declares the non-API `DATAPTR()` by default, so both instantiations of `simple2_()` fail to compile.

Reproduced locally against the R 4.6.1 headers: `DATAPTR was not declared in this scope`.

Failing CI: https://github.com/r-lib/covr/actions/runs/37270819359/job/111637222088

## Fix

- Pass the public `REAL()` or `INTEGER()` accessor as a compile-time template parameter.
- Retain the shared header template, its two compilation units, and existing coverage line numbers and expectations.
- Add a changelog entry; no legacy API opt-in or version-specific workaround.

## Verification

- All 26 assertions in the existing compiled-coverage tests pass on R 4.3.3 and R 4.6.1.
- `R CMD INSTALL --preclean --clean` successfully builds and loads `TestCompiled` on R 4.6.1.
- Native smoke calls for both double and integer specializations return `-1, 0, 1, 1` for inputs `-2, 0, 1, 2`.
- End-to-end `package_coverage()` on R 4.6.1 reports R coverage and the expected merged header counts `4, 3, 0, 1, 4` at lines 12, 18, 21, 23, 25.

The full R CMD check matrix was not run locally; the PR workflows will cover the remaining platforms and R versions.

title: Support for generating LCOV reports
Adds the simple codecov format to make using the codecov action easier
description:
As the codecov API has changed, direct uploads to codecov are currently somewhat flaky and might stop working in the future altogether when the old API endpoints are deactivated. A current workaround is using `to_cobertura` to generate a file and then upload it using the codecov action, which however introduces the `xml2` dependency (e.g. used in r-lib/covr#584 and r-lib/covr#568).
 
This PR proposes `to_simple_codecov` to solve this in a simpler way. The function returns the very simple [Codecov custom format](https://docs.codecov.com/docs/codecov-custom-coverage-format) (also seems similar (but not the same) to the existing codecov format). By writing this to a file we can upload the report via the GH action (on other services via the CLI) and do not have to worry about the API version anymore.

A codecov report based on a report file from `to_simple_codecov` can be found [here](https://app.codecov.io/github/pik-piam/magclass/commit/a18aab79b36f950b5853dfa489006f5e5d809b0a).

title: Account for vectors of length 0 when cleaning coverage
description:
Hi @jimhester, I'm sorry for bothering again. Apparently, my previous PR didn't cover an edge case of an edge case, or rather, by solving one, I created another. I'm sorry for that.

https://github.com/r-lib/covr/blob/f1866d296c00884d1f085ff245669de01bc864c4/R/covr.R#L669

`val` variable, in particular scenarios,  can have `integer(0)` value and because of this R behaviour:

```
> FALSE || logical(0)
[1] NA
```
we end up with an NA in the conditional. That's why I've rewritten the condition to use `length(val) == 0` instead of `is.null(val)`. It is more robust and covers more of the cases that are problematic for that function, because both `NULL` and `integer(0)` are of length 0. There should be no more problems with that function anymore. 

Closes #631

title: Fix rare count_test edge case (#2)
description:
Hi!

In our enterprise solution, we have discovered a peculiar edge case when `count_test` function is called with `.current_test` not yet initialized, leading to error:

```
Error in tests$.data[[1L]] <- .current_test$index : 
  replacement has length zero
```

For us, we encountered it when calculating coverage for the  `digest` when using `tinytest` Ubuntu libraries (funnily enough, when installing tinytest from source, the issue did not appear). That makes reproducing the issue really tedious, although I was able to do it on macOS as well. Nevertheless, I believe that there is no harm in adding that if statement to cover that edge case, even if it's super rare, simply to make sure the `covr` is not vulnerable to weird/unexpected package combinations in the future.

title: Fix bug when using non-absolute install_path
description:
Fixes #517 

This probably could be a bug to the tools package, but it is easy enough to fix here.

The tools bug is that when `install_path` is a relative path `tools::testInstalledPackages` has a failure when `type="examples"` and silently ignores all tests when `type="tests"`.


```r
path <- normalizePath(".")
package <- basename(path)
install_path <- "../temp_install_path"
out_dir <- file.path(install_path, package)

dir.create(install_path)
utils::install.packages(repos = NULL,
                        lib = install_path,
                        path,
                        type = "source",
                        INSTALL_opts = c("--example",
                                         "--install-tests",
                                         "--with-keep.source",
                                         "--with-keep.parse.data",
                                         "--no-staged-install",
                                         "--no-multiarch"),
                        quiet = FALSE)



# Fails (when both out_dir is set & install_path is set to a relative path)
tools::testInstalledPackage(package, outDir = out_dir, types = "examples", lib.loc = install_path)
#> Testing examples for package ‘covr’
#> Error in find.package(package, lib.loc) : 
#>   there is no package called ‘covr’

# Silently doesn't run any tests
tools::testInstalledPackage(package, outDir = out_dir, types = "tests", lib.loc = install_path)



# Need to normalize the install_path
normalized_install_path <- normalizePath(install_path)

# Works
tools::testInstalledPackage(package, outDir = out_dir, types = "examples", lib.loc = normalized_install_path)

# Works
tools::testInstalledPackage(package, outDir = out_dir, types = "tests", lib.loc = normalized_install_path)
```

title: parse_data: Fix compatibility with R 4.4
description:
This series resolves two issues with calculating package coverage under R 4.4:

 * for some packages, there is a substantial performance regression compared to R 4.3 (related to gh-567)

 * some packages hit into an error when applying exclusions (gh-576, gh-579)

In addition to the links above, there are cases demonstrating both these issues at <https://github.com/kyleam/covr-r44-issues>.

Here's a summary of timings (seconds, wall time) to give a sense of how severe the slowdown can be:

| package    | R 4.3.3 | R 4.4.2 | R 4.4.2 + patch |
|----------- |-------- |-------- |---------------- |
| data.table | 254     | 2290    | 235             |
| diffobj    | 231     | 1126    | 151             |
| R.utils    | 759     | 22197   | 599             |

("patch" refers to a run with a covr patched with the equivalent of the changes proposed here.)

---

Both the slowdown and error bisect to R's [990fe3d8a1](https://github.com/wch/r-source/commit/990fe3d8a10cca10e1181bd9ca41bbc8588b12f0) (getParseData() - for first-file objects ..., 2023-06-14).  And the [associated bug report](https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=16756) was actually connected to a covr PR (gh-154).

As discussed in the third commit's message, I think covr is getting tripped up by the new getParseData  returning parse data for the entire package.

<details>
<summary>example</summary>

Under R 4.4.1, `getParseData` returns the same result for `nanaduration` and `nanoival`, which are in separate files.  The parse data appears to be for all files of the package.

```R
d1 <- getParseData(nanotime::nanoduration)
d2 <- getParseData(nanotime::nanoival)

basename(attr(d1, "srcfile")[["filename"]])
#> [1] "nanoduration.R"
basename(attr(d2, "srcfile")[["filename"]])
#> [1] "nanoival.R"

attr(d1, "srcfile") <- NULL
attr(d2, "srcfile") <- NULL

identical(d1, d2)
#> [1] TRUE
```

</details>

I haven't worked out the details of how that leads to the `NA` values that trigger exclusions error.

My proposed solution is to reorder the `utils::getParseData` and `covr:::get_parse_data` calls so that `get_parse_data` is used for R 4.4 or greater, just as it is for R 4.3 or below.  As a result, the `get_tokens` call returns the expected per-file parse data.

The `utils::getParseData` call is retained as the fallback.  That's needed when not calculating *package* coverage (e.g., when calling `file_coverage`).

Putting `get_parse_data` in front of the `getParseData` call exposes two issues in `split_on_line_directives`.  Those are resolved in the first two commits.

Closes #576
Closes #579

cc: @dgkf @jimhester @krlmlr @mcol @MichaelChirico

title: Feature Enhancement: Minimize duplicated recorded tests
description:
Supersedes https://github.com/r-lib/covr/pull/530, Closes https://github.com/r-lib/covr/issues/528

The previous PR never got picked up and the repo has moved forward since then. This PR just rebases the changes onto the latest work in `covr`. Copying the original description below:

---

Refer to https://github.com/r-lib/covr/issues/528 for a detailed description of the issue, but in short the heuristic that was used for quickly determining whether we're evaluating a new test ended up being too specific, resulting in the same test being logged many times.

Generally this isn't an issue. Even in situations where a test suite might loop over a test, the heuristic would usually treat those as the same test. Even if it was logged with each iteration, those iteration counts are usually low enough that it doesn't impact the coverage object substantially. However, when testing `fastmap`, there were a couple cases where an expectation is made in a loop with 10s of thousands of iterations and logging the test with each evaluation, blowing up the coverage object memory needs.

To emphasize, these changes will only affect behaviors when `options(covr.record_tests = TRUE)`, which must be opted into.

title: Significant performance improvements for test recording (`options(covr.record_tests = TRUE)`)
description:
The impetus for these changes was a staggering performance hit when recording tests while running coverage against the `rlang` package. The low-level nature of the package meant that some traces were hit millions of times with very deep call stacks - a perfect stress test for this feature. 

Compared to vanilla coverage, I was originally seeing ~70x slowdown with this feature enabled. With these changes, I've brought that down to ~4x. Still not negligible, but much, much better.

Functionally, changes are pretty minor. A slight data structure rework and some reworks to minimize call stack unwinding where possible. Full details below, but I'll also annotate the major changes in the patch.

### Changes

A number of changes were introduced to reduce the performance overhead of recording tests as they hit traces. Three main changes were introduced. These were discovered primarily during the testing of the `rlang` package which is a good stress test for low-level behaviors.

1. `sys.nframe` and `sys.call` were used in place of `sys.calls` where possible, avoiding unnecessary unwrapping of the call stack. For packages whose tests result in deep call stacks, repeated `sys.calls` calls was a major bottleneck.

2. A single value `.current_test$record` is used instead of repeatedly extracting the setting from `getOption("covr.record_tests")`. Avoiding calls to `getOption` with each `count` call limits the performance impact on vanilla `covr`.

3. `.counters[[key]]$tests` was converted from a matrix to an environment containing a matrix to avoid reallocation on assignment. This results in a substantial (~5x) reduction in performance overhead.

4. `.counters[[key]]$tests$tally` (the matrix logging test hits) now initializes with 4 NA_integer_ records and doubles in size each time the available records are filled. This causes a substantial reduction in allocations during testing. For example: `rlang` hits some lines of code over 1M times during testing, which would reallocate a matrix as many times.  
    
    Because of this restructuring of the tests data, some of the consumers of this data were also refactored to handle this structure. In the spirit of keeping the `covr.record_tests` features maintainable, I also refactored many of the non-vanilla code branches into separate functions.

title: Filter long test calls from recorded tests (Closes #503)
description:
# Overview

This handles an edge case where exceptionally long test calls (> ~25K args) would throw a known segfault error with R's call deserialization from Rds. 

I raised the bug first with the R language, but it sounds like it would require more of a re-write than this extreme edge case warrants. If it's ever fixed, I also added in a canary to the testing suite to emit a warning to notify devs to skip this processing on fixed versions of R.

# Design Decisions

The one design decision that I would like to draw attention to is that I do this filtering for all traces, whether or not they write out to `Rds`. Since not all `.counters` go through a `Rds` file intermediate, this can be an unnecessary processing step in some cases. I chose to process traces in all cases regardless because I felt like it helped to keep a cleaner separation between `options(covr.record_tests = TRUE)` behaviors from the more general use case. Alternatively, this code could be tucked into `save_trace`, but it would add a fair bit of complexity that would have no effect in most cases (when `options(covr.record_tests = NULL)`).

title: Feature Addition (Addresses #462): Record test srcrefs and link to covr traces
description:
# Overview

As described in #462, this PR adds functionality to capture data about the executing test while capturing coverage traces. This adds two pieces of additional data to the coverage object:

### `attr(,"tests")`

During collection, this is captured under `.counters$tests` (the `.counters` environment namespace uses srcref "keys" as names, so the `test` name can be confidently used without risk of conflicts.) This object is lifted out into an attribute in `package_coverage`. It includes curated calls from the call stack during the execution of a test. Calls are included if their source is within the tests directory or is the last call prior to entering the package namespace (before the first `count` call).  

```r
options(covr.record_tests = TRUE)
cov <- covr::package_coverage(testthat::test_path("testFunctional"))
attr(cov, "tests")
# $`./test-a.R:2:3:2:25:3:25:2:2`
# $`./test-a.R:2:3:2:25:3:25:2:2`[[1]]
# test_that("regular function `a` works as expected", {
#   expect_equal(a(), TRUE)
#   expect_equal(b(), FALSE)
# })
# 
# $`./test-a.R:2:3:2:25:3:25:2:2`[[2]]
# expect_equal(a(), TRUE)
# 
# $`./test-a.R:2:3:2:25:3:25:2:2`[[3]]
# a()
# 
# 
# $`./test-a.R:3:3:3:26:3:26:3:3`
# $`./test-a.R:3:3:3:26:3:26:3:3`[[1]]
# test_that("regular function `a` works as expected", {
#   expect_equal(a(), TRUE)
#   expect_equal(b(), FALSE)
# })
# 
# $`./test-a.R:3:3:3:26:3:26:3:3`[[2]]
# expect_equal(b(), FALSE)
# 
# $`./test-a.R:3:3:3:26:3:26:3:3`[[3]]
# b()
```

### `<coverage object>$<srcref key>$tests`

In addition, each covr trace keeps a listing of which tests result in the trace execution including the index of the corresponding tests in `attr(cov, "tests")` and the stack depth into the package at which the trace is executed:

```r
cov$`a.R:6:7:6:18:7:18:8:8`$tests
#      test depth
# [1,]    1     1
```

## Change log

- Added [`covr.record_tests` option](https://github.com/dgkf/covr/blob/c32d9aee3c43794686e375a9d21478d596d814a6/R/covr.R#L69-L71), which must be `TRUE` before additional information is used
- Added [call to `count_test`](https://github.com/dgkf/covr/blob/c32d9aee3c43794686e375a9d21478d596d814a6/R/trace_calls.R#L108-L136) from `count`, if option "covr.record_tests" is `TRUE`
- Added [`.current_test` environment object](https://github.com/dgkf/covr/blob/c32d9aee3c43794686e375a9d21478d596d814a6/R/trace_calls.R#L106) to the `covr` namespace (like `.counters`), which is used for capturing the current test during each trace count. It is invalidated if the executing call srcref changes and a new test trace, test frame and srcref take its place as the current test.
- Introduced an internal [`as_coverage`](https://github.com/dgkf/covr/blob/c32d9aee3c43794686e375a9d21478d596d814a6/R/covr.R#L109-L127) function, in order to centralize handling of the .counters$test value.
- [Made `merge_coverage` an S3 generic function](https://github.com/dgkf/covr/blob/c32d9aee3c43794686e375a9d21478d596d814a6/R/covr.R#L529-L534), dispatching on a character vector of filepaths or a list of coverage objects. This just makes it [easier to test](https://github.com/dgkf/covr/blob/c32d9aee3c43794686e375a9d21478d596d814a6/tests/testthat/test-record_tests.R#L121) without having to write coverage objects out to files. 
- [Added handling for `<coverage obj>$tests` consolidation in `merge_coverage`](https://github.com/dgkf/covr/blob/c32d9aee3c43794686e375a9d21478d596d814a6/R/covr.R#L552-L565)
- [Added new insertion into package startup](https://github.com/dgkf/covr/blob/c32d9aee3c43794686e375a9d21478d596d814a6/R/covr.R#L653), propagating `options(covr.record_tests = .(getOption("covr.record_tests")))` through to package startup within a test installation.
- [Added itemization of `covr` options](https://github.com/dgkf/covr/blob/c32d9aee3c43794686e375a9d21478d596d814a6/R/covr.R#L19-L74) to `?covr` package documentation. This isn't directly related to test srcrefs, but seemed like a gap I could address in the process. I tried my best to document the options whose behavior, pulling comments where they exist already somewhere in the code base when possible or when I could confidently infer from the source code. There were quite a few (mostly pertaining to gcc and icc) that I left blank. 
- Updated NEWS
- Bumped version number (roxygen version also got bumped to 7.1.1 while I was rebuilding the package, can revert if needed, but I'd need to downgrade my roxygen install to rebuild docs). 

# Design Considerations 

Just a couple design decisions that I want to raise to your attention for review:
1. I use `$tests` within `.counters`. I think this is safe, knowing that srcref keys will always take the form `a:1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8`, but it's always a bit disconcerting to attribute so much meaning to value names. 
2. Is there perhaps [a better way to propagate options to the child environment](https://github.com/dgkf/covr/blob/c32d9aee3c43794686e375a9d21478d596d814a6/R/covr.R#L652-L656) in which tests are executed?

# Benchmarks

I did a bit of benchmarking. Across the board, execution time was about 5-10% slower with `options(covr.record_tests)` enabled, and object size (using `lobstr::obj_size`) was ~5x the size. 

# Future Work

- There's room for improvement in how it handles packages tested with RUnit (more work needed to effectively build a test trace)
- Continue to test on a wider sampling of packages

Hotfix: Fix regression in how test depth is calculated; add exec index
description:
This is a little bit of a dual part PR - first a fix to a regression introduced over the course of preparing #463, and the other piece is a small feature enhancement that enables a lot of powerful functionality.

### Depth calculation fix

Between the initial PR for #463 to the final commit, I went from just recording the final test frame to instead recording the entire test call stack up until the first `covr::count` call. Unfortunately, I forgot to update the way that the stack depth of the test trace was calculated. This has been fixed now by taking the length of the stack trace, instead of (what was) the index of the frame to begin on.

```diff
-  depth_into_pkg <- length(sys.calls()) - .current_test$frame - n_calls_into_covr + 1L
+  depth_into_pkg <- length(sys.calls()) - length(.current_test$frames) - n_calls_into_covr + 1L
```

Unfortunately, this was silently causing incorrect depth because of `rbind`'s value recycling. (effectively doing the same as `rbind(c(1, 2), c(3, NULL))`) ([location in diff](https://github.com/r-lib/covr/compare/master...dgkf:hotfix/test-trace-depth?expand=1#diff-d9130936e59a1de9d8ecb0695b16876ae6557ca3a23c80213d24d4574e07cf89R107)).

All is good now, and I added in some tests to avoid this from happening in the future.

### Feature Addition: Test execution index

As well, I added in an index for each trace. I'm pretty excited to have this introduced. Although it's just a tiny bit of added information, it effectively means that we can reconstruct the execution path that a test took while evaluating which opens up a lot of opportunities for analyzing the test traces. 

In practice we get something like this (below), where `i` records the order in which each trace is executed by each test. Combining this matrix across traces and sorting by "test" and "i" would let us see the order of coverage counts executed by a test. 

```
#' # $`source.Ref2326138c55:3:8:3:8:8:8:3:3`
#' #      test depth i
#' # [1,]    1     1 1
#' # [2,]    1     2 3
```

Materially, this means storing an extra column to the tests matrix for each trace. It comes at no substantial computational or object size cost.

---

- [x] Updated `?covr.record_tests` documentation to describe new data column
- [x] Added tests
- [x] Bumped DESCRIPTION dev version
- [x] Added reference to PR in NEWS entry regarding these changes

title: [hotfix] Nested coverage execution using covr.record_tests=TRUE (#463)
description:
In using the `covr.record_test` feature added in #463 for testing, I discovered that it's possible to end up in a scenario where `covr` is tracing `covr:::count` calls from multiple packages by running `package_coverage` within a testing suite. In the case where the outer package's tests were not being record, but the inner package's tests are, then these `count` calls from the outer package will attempt to record tests despite not having the necessary fields in the `.counters[[key]]`. 

This fix adds a simple check for whether these fields are present before trying to append to them, which fixes the issues I've encountered while trying to run nested coverage runs for testing. 

Additionally, I've rebuilt the docs which added my name to the package Rd.

description:
I would please like to suggest the following small fix.

In running covr::package_coverage() I was seeing the following:

```
  warnings()
  Warning messages:
   1: In rm(nme, envir = package_parse_data) : object 'nme' not found
   2: In rm(nme, envir = package_parse_data) : object 'nme' not found
```
  
Looking into cover R/parse_data.R I see the code:

```
  clean_parse_data <- function() {
    for (nme in ls(package_parse_data)) {
      rm(nme, envir = package_parse_data)
    }
  }
```
  
The rm() statement is attempting to remove an object named "nme", not the object named by the variable nme.  I suggest the following replacement code:

```
  clean_parse_data <- function() {
    rm(list = ls(package_parse_data), envir = package_parse_data)
  }
```
  
This pull request is entirely the above change.

I ran devtools::test() before the change, and after the change.  I observed no change for the worse.  I also confirmed the warnings went away and I could run package_coverage().


Tests before:

```
Duration: 42.6 s

OK:       256
Failed:   6
Warnings: 0
Skipped:  0
```


Tests after:

```
Duration: 40.2 s

OK:       256
Failed:   6
Warnings: 0
Skipped:  0
```

Thank you for the package and thank you for your time.

description:
I have had issues with Coveralls not listing my jobs, although they are created and uploaded.  This currently only occurs for one of my many repository.
- R.oo list of jobs: https://coveralls.io/r/HenrikBengtsson/R.oo (~~completely empty~~)
- R.oo coverage job: https://coveralls.io/jobs/4187059

Searching the web, there are several reports on this (e.g. https://github.com/lemurheavy/coveralls-public/issues/281) and yet have to find an answer/solution to the problem. 

So, in the efforts on troubleshooting this one, I wanted to see what coverage 'covr' uploads from Travis CI, which is why I added support for `covr::coveralls(quiet=TRUE)`, e.g. see end of https://travis-ci.org/HenrikBengtsson/R.oo/builds/48542721.

I kept it backward compatibility, hence the default `quiet=FALSE`.
## UPDATE

Just adding these notes here in case someone else have similar problems and discovers this post.  I first discovered that Coveralls listed several files to have "no data" within each jobs.  Then manually going through those, I discovered that the files for which data was missing where all alphabetically at the beginning, and then "all of a sudden" the remaining files had data. I also discovered that the last file for which data did not exist, linked to a broken page on Coveralls, i.e. the link for `R/equals.default.R` listed by [R.oo job 38.1](https://coveralls.io/jobs/4188393) is [broken](https://coveralls.io/files/444656217).  I added an explicit test for function, but that made no difference - the link to that file is still [broken](https://coveralls.io/files/444765102) in [R.oo job 39.1](https://coveralls.io/jobs/4189460).  Interestingly, the covr output (using `quiet=FALSE`) also show that that file has [zero coverage](https://travis-ci.org/HenrikBengtsson/R.oo/builds/48563210), which it shouldn't have.

Now, here's the really interesting part.  In the next iteration/commit/push, I added test cases for another file, R/ASCII.R, which is ahead in alphabetic sense.  Nothing else was done, cf. R.oo Commit [81b1232](https://github.com/HenrikBengtsson/R.oo/commit/81b12322120017859cefe223f4526e51a83bc0f9).  That file now reports 100% coverage, but more importantly that triggered covr to all of a sudden also report [100%](https://travis-ci.org/HenrikBengtsson/R.oo/builds/48564405) for `R/equals.default.R`.

From this I am starting to believe this issue has to do with 'covr' et al. rather than Coveralls.  It's seems that the internal coverage data somehow can become broken which is revealed both by `print()` but also what is uploaded to Coveralls.

Phew.

readChar(..., useBytes=FALSE) in UTF-8 encodings is not safe
description:
`covr:::to_coveralls()` uses `readChar()` to read all the source code files, with the default `useBytes=FALSE`.  However, it is not safe to use `readChar(..., useBytes=FALSE)` on source code files **iff** the encoding is UTF-8, because **source code comments may contain invalid UTF-8 byte sequences**, e.g. French accents in Latin-9 encodings.  This is ok according to current R standards.  See R-devel thread '[SUGGESTION: Force install.packages() to use ASCII encoding when parse():ing code?](https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-devel/2014-December/070274.html)' on 2014-12-11 for full details.

REPRODUCIBLE EXAMPLE:
Add a Swedish/German ö (an o with "umlaut") to a source code comment and using Latin-9 file encoding (non-multibyte) as in https://github.com/HenrikBengtsson/rmini/blob/99b93/R/hello.R will cause `readChar(..., useBytes=FALSE)` to choke if `options(encoding="UTF-8")` as seen in Lines 913-919 in https://travis-ci.org/HenrikBengtsson/rmini/builds/46643665.

PATCH:
This pull request simply uses `useBytes=TRUE`, which covers all R code per se, because according to R docs code itself can only be in ASCII (it's only the source code comments that can be of any (mixed?) encoding).  This avoids the problem, cf. https://travis-ci.org/HenrikBengtsson/rmini/builds/46644001.  Not sure where that remaining

```
Warning message:
grepl("\n", lines, fixed = TRUE):
  input string 1 is invalid in this locale
```

originates from, but it is most likely related to the fact that the source code contains invalid byte sequences if parsed as UTF-8.  It could also be from `devtools` or from R itself.  At least it doesn't give an error.

The downside to using `useBytes=TRUE` is multi-byte characters in source code comments may not look as expected over at Coveralls, e.g. https://coveralls.io/files/420031823 compare with https://github.com/HenrikBengtsson/rmini/blob/99b93/R/hello.R.  On the other hand, I don't see another solution to handle the current "fragile" R specs.

description:
Supersedes #559 by @gergness, reworked to address the review in https://github.com/r-lib/covr/pull/559#issuecomment-3497808785.

`package_coverage(show_code_output = TRUE)` shows the output of `code` on the console while it runs (e.g. to follow it in CI logs), instead of only showing it when it fails.

## How it works

- The code runs with `R --vanilla --quiet -f <file>`, not `Rscript`, so it gets the same default packages, environment and echoed commands as the current `R CMD BATCH` run.
- It is started with `sys::exec_wait()`. sys is already a hard transitive dependency (httr → openssl → askpass → sys), and is now listed in `Imports`. The child's stdout and stderr go to separate callbacks: each chunk is printed to the console's stdout or stderr respectively, so the two streams stay separate, and is also written to the usual `<pkg>-commands.Rout.fail` file. Failures still go through `show_failures()`, so the user gets a `covr_error` with `$file`/`$output`, and `allow_failures = TRUE` still works.
- No shell is involved (so there is no cmd.exe quoting on Windows) and the exit status comes from sys, so it works on every supported R version.
- The saved file has both streams, as `R CMD BATCH`'s does. The order of chunks that arrive at about the same time can differ from the order the child wrote them in, as they are read from two pipes.

## Tests

- New tests in `test-package_coverage.R` check the exact stdout and stderr shown on the console, that coverage is measured, and that a failure is a `covr_error` with the saved output.
- I checked by hand that output appears as it is printed and not all at the end.
- `R CMD check` passes, apart from 2 environment notes.

Fixes #558

title: Don't pass covr's library paths as site libraries
description:
Fixes #560.
Fixes #571.

## Cause

vetiver embeds a copy of renv (`vetiver/inst/vendor/renv.R`, loaded from vetiver's `.onLoad`). Whenever renv loads, its `renv_sandbox_init()` checks every library path for a `.renv-sandbox` marker. If it finds one, it activates the sandbox, which removes the site libraries (`.Library.site`) and the system library from `.libPaths()` (rstudio/renv#1565).

`package_coverage()` passes the current `.libPaths()` to the R processes that run the tests, and in an renv project those paths include the renv sandbox. It also set `R_LIBS_SITE` to all of these library paths, so in those processes every library was a site library. When the package imports vetiver (or renv), loading it removed every library except the sandbox before the instrumented package's load script ran `covr:::register_trace()`. That's the error in the issue:

```
> library(covr.test)
Error in loadNamespace(x) : there is no package called 'covr'
```

Library paths in a test process, before and after `loadNamespace("renv")`, run from an renv project:

| `R_LIBS_SITE` | `.libPaths()` after loading renv |
| --- | --- |
| all of covr's libraries (before) | only the renv sandbox |
| site libraries of the session, `"NULL"` (after) | renv project library and sandbox |

## Fix

The processes now get the current session's `.Library.site` as `R_LIBS_SITE`, which is what callr does. When there are no site libraries, as in renv projects, they get `"NULL"` (an empty value would mean the default site library). `R_LIBS` and `R_LIBS_USER` still contain all of the library paths, so the libraries the processes see don't change, and examples, where `tools::testInstalledPackage()` clears `R_LIBS`, still find them through `R_LIBS_USER`.

## Verification

- I reproduced the issue in a local renv project with a package that has `import(vetiver)` (vetiver 0.2.8) and another with `importFrom(renv, paths)`. Both failed with `there is no package called 'covr'`, and both get 100% coverage with this branch installed.
- New test: the code run by `package_coverage()` starts a process that removes the site libraries from the library paths the way renv does, then loads the package. It fails without the fix and passes with it. It's skipped on R < 4.1.0 (no `include.site`) and when covr itself is installed in a site library.
- `devtools::test()` with this version installed: 775 passed, 0 failed.

title: Add a dark theme to report() and file_report()
description:
`report()` and `file_report()` now use a dark theme when the browser prefers one, and have a "Dark mode" button to switch themes.

- **Auto-detection:** `inst/www/theme.js` is inlined in the `<head>`, so the page never flashes the wrong theme on load. It reads `prefers-color-scheme` and follows changes to it while the page is open. It adds the `dark` class to `<html>`, which DataTables 1.13 already uses for its own dark styles.
- **Toggle:** The button sets `aria-pressed`. The choice goes into `localStorage`, so other open reports and new ones use it too. Switching back to the browser's preference clears the stored choice, so the report follows the browser again. If storage isn't available, the toggle still works for the current page.
- **Colors:** The coverage bars in the file list now use CSS variables (`--covr-bar-high/mid/low`) instead of hard-coded colors in the DataTables callback. In the dark theme, the `covr.report_colors` colors are mixed with the dark background. The light theme's colors are unchanged. Syntax highlighting in the dark theme uses colors based on Tomorrow Night.

I checked this in headless Chromium on a demo package with 40%, 83% and 94% coverage, using the default colors and the blue/orange `covr.report_colors`:

- the theme follows the emulated dark and light preference
- the choice survives a reload and carries over to `file_report()`
- switching back to the preference clears the stored value

`file_report()` already logged `Bootstrap's JavaScript requires jQuery` before this change, because it doesn't load jQuery, so its syntax highlighting doesn't run. That still happens and isn't fixed here.

Fixes #563.

```r

```
