title: Document running testthat tests with snapshots under coverage
description:
Fixes #501.

`file_coverage()` runs test files with `sys.source()`, so the `test_that()` blocks run without testthat's runner: `expect_snapshot()` can't compare against a snapshot (and is skipped as an empty test), and testthat uses its 2nd edition, so on current testthat `expect_snapshot()` errors unless the test calls `local_edition(3)`.

This adds a "testthat tests" section to `?file_coverage` showing how to run such tests with `with_coverage()` (#655) and `testthat::test_file(env = env)` instead.

Verified with testthat 3.3.2 and the issue's example: `file_coverage()` gives 66.67% but skips the snapshot; the documented `with_coverage()` pattern with `NOT_CRAN=true` creates `tests/_snaps/temp_fn.md` on the first run, passes on the second, and reports a snapshot failure after changing the function's output, with the same 66.67% coverage.

title: Add `covr.report_colors` option for report colors
description:
`report()`, `file_report()` and the coverage percentages printed in the console now read the colors for covered and missed code from a new `covr.report_colors` option. This lets people with color vision deficiency replace the default green and red:

```r
options(covr.report_colors = c(covered = "#0072B2", missed = "#E69F00"))  # blue / orange
```

Fixes #529.

## Why an option and not an argument

- You set it once, e.g. in `.Rprofile`, and every report uses it. That suits a color-vision preference better than passing an argument on each call.
- It also works for the RStudio "Calculate package test coverage" addin, which calls `report()` with no arguments.
- It covers `report()` and `file_report()` with one setting, and it fits the existing `covr.*` options that are documented in `?covr`.

## Details

- The value is a named character vector with `covered` and/or `missed` elements. Each element can be any R color that `grDevices::col2rgb()` accepts. If you leave one out, it keeps its default.
- The colors apply everywhere the report uses them:
  - line backgrounds (30% alpha)
  - the hovered line-number cell (70% alpha)
  - the hover underline shadow
  - the coverage bars in the Files tab, drawn as light tints of the chosen colors
- The color rules moved from `inst/www/report.css` into a `<style>` block generated in R. With the option unset, the CSS values and the coverage-bar JS are byte-for-byte the same as before. This was checked by diffing the report from `main` against the report from this branch.
- `report()` checks the option before running `package_coverage()`. A bad value fails right away with a clear error: an unnamed vector, unknown names, a non-character value, or an invalid color name.
- An optional `partial` element sets the color of partial coverage (75% to 90%): the console percentages in that range and the middle tier of the Files-tab bars. It's named `partial` so it can also be used once covr reports partially covered lines. Without it, that band keeps today's yellow, or uses `covered` when that is set.
- Console `print()`: percentages of 90% or more and of 75% or more use the `covered` color, and lower ones use `missed`, via `cli::make_ansi_style()`. Colors that aren't set keep today's ANSI green/yellow/red, so the default output is unchanged.
- The Files-tab bars now use the console's thresholds (`>= 90` / `>= 75` instead of `> 90` / `> 75`), so the two agree. Files at exactly 75% or 90% coverage get the higher color in the report.
- An invalid `covr.report_colors` makes `report()` / `file_report()` stop, but `print()` only warns and falls back to the default colors, so coverage objects still print.
- Transparency in colors is ignored. In terminals with only 8 colors, the console uses the closest of those (documented).
- `grDevices` is added to Imports for `col2rgb()`. It is a base package.

## Tests

- New tests in `tests/testthat/test-report.R`:
  - the default colors appear unchanged in the HTML
  - custom colors appear in the `report()` and `file_report()` HTML, and none of the default colors are left
  - setting only one color works
  - validation errors are covered by snapshots
- New test in `tests/testthat/test-print.R`: `format_percentage()` uses the chosen colors, and colors that aren't set keep the defaults.
- Full suite, with this branch installed first: `[ FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 1 | PASS 668 ]`.
- Checked by rendering a blue/orange report in Chromium. The computed backgrounds were `rgba(0, 114, 178, 0.3)` for covered lines and `rgba(230, 159, 0, 0.3)` for missed lines, and the coverage bar had the orange tint.

title: Upload to Codecov with the current upload protocol
description:
`codecov()` now uploads with the protocol used by the Codecov CLI and `codecov/codecov-action`, instead of the legacy `/upload/v2` endpoint, which Codecov documents as unmaintained, rate limits without a token, and which does not support organization-level (global) upload tokens.

Fixes #568.
Fixes #464.

## Protocol

1. `POST <base_url>/upload/<git service>/<owner>::::<repo>/upload-coverage` with a JSON body (`ci_service`, `ci_url`, `cli_args`, `env`, `flags`, `job_code`, `name`, `version`, `file_not_found`, `branch`, `code`, `commitid`, `parent_commit_id`, `pullid`) and, if there is a token, `Authorization: token <token>`. The response has `raw_upload_location` and `url`.
2. `PUT raw_upload_location` with `{report_fixes, network_files, coverage_files, metadata}`. The coverage file is covr's existing JSON from `to_codecov()` (processed by Codecov's `RlangProcessor`), sent as `coverage.json` in the format `base64+compressed`.

## Design

- The per-CI detection of commit, branch, PR, job, build URL and slug is kept and mapped to the new fields (`job_code` is the former `job`, or `build` when there was no job). GitLab CI is also detected from `GITLAB_CI` and its current variables.
- Slug: from the CI (`GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `CI_PROJECT_PATH`, `TRAVIS_REPO_SLUG`, ...), otherwise parsed from `git remote get-url origin`. Nested groups are encoded as `group:::subgroup::::repo`.
- Git service: `github` / `github_enterprise` on GitHub Actions, `gitlab` / `gitlab_enterprise` on GitLab CI, otherwise from the host of the `origin` remote, defaulting to `github`.
- `base_url` defaults to `https://ingest.codecov.io`; the former default `https://codecov.io` (and `https://app.codecov.io`) is replaced by it. Other values (Enterprise) are used as given.
- The token lookup order is unchanged: argument, `CODECOV_TOKEN`, `codecov.yml`. An empty `CODECOV_TOKEN` now falls through to `codecov.yml` as documented.
- Tokenless uploads need an unprotected branch. On GitHub Actions, with no token, no explicit `branch` and a pull request from a fork (`pull_request.head.repo.full_name` in `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` differs from `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`), the branch becomes the head label `owner:branch`, as `codecov/codecov-action` does. Same-repository pull requests and other CI services keep the plain branch.
- Codecov's serializer rejects null for `flags`, `ci_service` and `version`, so `flags` is `[]` when there are none and `ci_service` is `"local"` outside recognised CI services (as the Codecov CLI sends); the other fields are nullable server side.
- On GitHub Actions pull requests the commit is the head commit of the pull request from the event, rather than `GITHUB_SHA` (the merge commit), as `codecov/codecov-action` does.
- Errors follow #672 for both requests: 4xx is an error of class `covr_codecov_error` containing Codecov's response text, 429/5xx is a warning of class `covr_codecov_warning` and `codecov()` returns `NULL`. On success `codecov()` returns the parsed response of the first request (including `url`) invisibly, and prints the url when `quiet = FALSE`.
- `?codecov` documents the protocol, tokens (including organization-level tokens), tokenless uploads, and recommends `covr::to_lcov()` plus `codecov/codecov-action` as an alternative.

## Verification

- New tests (mocking covr's `RETRY` and git helpers) cover the request URL and slug encoding, the `Authorization` header present/absent, the JSON body for each CI, GitHub Actions push, same-repo and fork pull requests (unprotected branch), the payload decoding (base64, then zlib decompress) back to `to_codecov()` output, and the error/warning paths of both requests. The legacy-query tests and snapshots are removed.
- Against a local mock server, with the installed package: the `POST` went to `/upload/github/r-lib::::covr/upload-coverage` with `Authorization: token ...` and a JSON body; the `PUT` went to `raw_upload_location` with no `Authorization` and no `Content-Type`; the payload's coverage file decoded with Python's `base64` and `zlib.decompress` to valid JSON identical to `to_codecov()` (`memCompress(type = "gzip")` writes a zlib stream, `78 9c` header).
- Against the real `https://ingest.codecov.io` the first request is routed and a 404 (`{"message":"Repository not found"}`) is reported as a `covr_codecov_error`; no coverage was uploaded.
- Full test suite with the branch installed: `FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 1 | PASS 710`.

The real end-to-end check is this PR's own test-coverage job, which calls `covr::codecov()` with covr's repository `CODECOV_TOKEN`.

title: Add `c()` method for coverage objects
description:
Adds an exported `c.coverage()` method to combine coverage objects, e.g. coverage from tests in `tests/testthat` and slower tests in another directory:

```r
cov <- c(
  package_coverage(),
  package_coverage(type = "none", code = "testthat::test_dir('tests/local')")
)
```

It is a thin wrapper around the internal `merge_coverage()`, which stays internal:

- Each coverage object is converted to the raw trace list form (`attr(, "tests")` moved into a `$tests` element, per-trace test matrices wrapped as `$tests$tally`), merged, and converted back.
- Counts of shared traces are added; traces in only one object are appended.
- Tests recorded with `options(covr.record_tests = TRUE)` are combined and renumbered.
- The result keeps the first object's attributes (`package`, `root`, `library`, …) and the union of `attr(, "excluded_lines")`.
- Arguments that aren't coverage objects, or coverage of different packages (by `attr(, "package")$package`), signal a `covr_combine_error`. Objects without a package (`file_coverage()`, `code_coverage()`) can be combined with each other.
- No `c()` method for `coverages` objects.

Docs note that S3 dispatch only happens when the first argument is a coverage object; the example combines two `file_coverage()` runs.

Tests: shared traces summed (and `tally_coverage()`/`percent_coverage()` reflect it), disjoint traces appended, attributes/excluded lines, recorded tests renumbered, different-package and non-coverage errors. Full suite run with the branch installed: `[ FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 1 | PASS 643 ]`; `pkgdown::check_pkgdown()` clean.

Fixes #439.

title: Tally coverage by function
description:
`tally_coverage()` gains `by = "function"`, which returns one row for each top level R function with the columns `filename`, `functions`, `first_line`, `last_line` and `value`. `value` is the largest execution count of the function's expressions, so a function counts as covered if any of its code ran. Compiled code has no function names, so it is left out.

Because `zero_coverage()`, `percent_coverage()` and `print()` pass `by` through to `tally_coverage()`, `zero_coverage(cov, by = "function")` now lists the functions that were never run, `percent_coverage(cov, by = "function")` gives the percentage of functions run, and `print(cov, by = "function")` the percentage per file.

Fixes #245.

title: Report gcov's diagnostics when gcov fails
description:
Investigating #537 showed that no version of gcov exits nonzero for an object that genuinely has no functions. gcc 9–11 always exit 0. gcc >= 12 set a nonzero status only for real failures: 1 or 2 when the notes file can't be opened or isn't a notes file, 3 for a version mismatch, 4 for corruption, 5 for a stamp mismatch and 6 for output errors (see `read_graph_file()` and `read_count_file()` in `gcc/gcov.cc`). `executed_summary()` prints `No executable lines` either way. Status 3 together with `no functions found` and `No executable lines` is exactly what a `.gcno` version mismatch produces (reproduced with gcov 13 by patching a `.gcno` version). That means the package was compiled with a different gcc than the gcov covr runs.

So instead of ignoring the failure, `run_gcov()` now runs gcov through `gcov_run()`. It captures gcov's stdout and stderr and includes them in the error, e.g.:

```
Error: gcov failed (3):
./data.gcno:version '*31B', prefer 'B33*'
./data.gcno:no functions found
./data.gcda:cannot open data file, assuming not executed
No executable lines
```

Previously the error was just `Command ... failed (3)`, and gcov's stderr was lost when `quiet = TRUE`.

Verified:
- `package_coverage()` on `TestCompiled` plus a data-only `src/data.c` succeeds with the real gcov 13.
- It fails with the message above when run through a gcov wrapper that introduces a version mismatch.
- Regression tests cover `No executable lines` combined with missing, invalid, version-mismatched and corrupted notes files.
- The full suite passes with the branch installed.

Fixes #537.

title: Make `trace_environment()` idempotent
description:
Re-tracing an already traced namespace (e.g. when `pkgload::load_all()` re-fires the onLoad hook) no longer clears the counters or re-instruments instrumented functions. `exclude()` now also tolerates traces with `NA` line numbers.

Fixes #641.

title: Fix test-coverage job: don't use skip_on_covr() in tests
description: The test-coverage job on main fails since #692: `shim_package.sh` renames `skip_on_covr()` to `skip_on_covrShim()`, which doesn't exist. This checks `R_COVR` directly, which the shim leaves alone. Verified locally: the shimmed covr-on-covr run with `CI=true` now completes.

title: Exclude the Rcpp interfaces header from coverage
description:
`package_coverage()` now excludes `inst/include/<pkg>_RcppExports.h`, generated by Rcpp for `// [[Rcpp::interfaces(cpp)]]`, like the other files generated by Rcpp and cpp11.

Fixes #531.

title: Make `options(covr.gcov = "")` turn off compiled code coverage
description:
A missing gcov is now represented as `NA`, so it still errors when there are `.gcno` files, while an explicit `""` skips gcov as documented.

Fixes #516.

title: Compute line coverage the same way in every output
description:
Fixes #620.

## Problem

`per_line()` (used by `report()`, `codecov()`, `coveralls()`) and `tally_coverage()` (used by `print()`, `percent_coverage()`, `coverage_to_list()`, `to_cobertura()`, `to_sonarqube()`, `to_lcov()`) computed line coverage differently:

- For a line inside a multi-line expression, `per_line()` kept the value of the **last** expression on the line. In the issue, line 177 sits inside an expression spanning 176-178 and has `is.logical(x)` (196), `any(x)` (0) and `sum(x)` (196), so `report()` showed 196 while `tally_coverage()` showed 0.
- `tally_coverage()` has a row for each function on a line, and `percent_coverage()`, `print()`, `coverage_to_list()`, Cobertura and SonarQube counted those rows separately, so a line shared by two functions counted twice. `to_lcov()` already merged them.
- `tally_coverage()` counted lines that only contain punctuation, such as `}` and `})`, but `per_line()` dropped them (#387).

## Change

There is now one rule: a line counts as covered only if every expression on it ran.

- `tally_lines()` gives each line the **minimum** count of the expressions on it, using only the innermost expressions on that line (`innermost_lines()`). An enclosing multi-line expression only counts for lines that no expression inside it is on. Without this, `lapply(x, function(i) {...})` would lower the counts of the closure body. Worse, a closure created when the package was installed (`TestFunctional`) would make lines that ran show as uncovered. The existing #387 test covers that case. This is a change to `tally_coverage()`: before, the enclosing expression's count took part in the minimum.
  - Source ranges of parsed code are nested or disjoint, so there is no self-join. `nesting_parents()` sorts the ranges by start, longest first, and finds the range directly containing each one with a stack in a single pass. An expression is then dropped only from the lines of the expressions directly inside it. The cost is linear in the number of expressions plus lines, rather than k² for k expressions on one line.
- `non_code_lines()` drops blank, comment-only and punctuation-only lines for `tally_coverage()`, using the rule `per_line()` used. It replaces `source_blank_lines()` and `srcfile_lines()`, which only handled blank and comment lines of `.R` files.
- `per_line()` is now built on `tally_coverage()`, which replaces the row-by-row loop.
- `collapse_lines()` (formerly `lcov_lines()`) makes one row per line with the minimum over functions. `percent_coverage()` (when tallying by line), `print()` grouped by file, `coverage_to_list()`, `to_cobertura()` (totals and class lines; method lines stay per function), `to_sonarqube()` and `to_lcov()` all use it.

`to_sonarqube()` still leaves out compiled code (lines with no function), as before.

## Note on the test case

The test fixture (`shared_line_coverage()` in `helper.R`) uses the issue's line, `if (is.logical(x)) any(x) else sum(x)`, inside a multi-line `lapply()` call, and calls `f()` with **integers**, so `any(x)` never runs. That matches the issue's data. If `f()` is called only with a logical, the expression that never runs is the last one on the line. The old `per_line()` already reported that case as uncovered, so the test would pass before the fix. The line also has to be inside a multi-line expression, because otherwise the old code took the minimum. Every new test fails on `main` and passes here.

Reported line coverage may go down slightly (NEWS bullet added). `percent_coverage` in `test-summary.R` now expects 80% instead of 83.3%, because the `})` line no longer counts.

## Verification

- Full suite with the branch installed (`R CMD INSTALL -l $CL .; R_LIBS=$CL devtools::test()`): all pass.
- `per_line()` and `tally_coverage()` agree on every line of `TestFunctional`, `TestS4` and `TestCompiled`.
- Timing for k expressions on one line inside a multi-line expression:

  | k | earlier self-join | sweep |
  | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | 1,000 | 2.1 s | 0.01 s |
  | 4,000 | 39 s | 0.07 s |
  | 100,000 | — | 0.54 s |

  The new test `tally_coverage() is fast with thousands of expressions on a line` uses 2,000 expressions and a 2 s limit. It fails on the earlier self-join commit; at 5,000 expressions the self-join went over a 4 GB memory cap.
- Equivalence check (throwaway script): on 725 expressions from covr's own `R/` files, plus `TestFunctional`, `TestS4` and `TestCompiled`, with random counts, the sweep gives exactly the same rows as the earlier self-join.
- The new shared-line tests for `to_lcov()`, `coverage_to_markdown()` and the `codecov()` and `coveralls()` payloads (upload mocked) fail on `main` and pass here.

title: Fix `report()` on empty coverage
description:
`compute_file_stats()` returned `NULL` for zero files, so `sort_file_stats()` failed on `-stats$Relevant`. Return a zero-row data frame with the expected columns instead.

Fixes #540.

Note: this fixes the empty-coverage reporting error in #540; the original reason `package_coverage()` returned zero traces was not reproduced (the reporter's package now gives 3 traces with covr 3.6.5).

title: Don't record environments of functions in test calls
description:
With `options(covr.record_tests = TRUE)`, the recorded test calls come from `sys.calls()`, and those can contain functions instead of function names:

- R evaluates an active binding by building a call with the binding's function itself in the function position (`getActiveValue()` in `src/main/envir.c`). An R6 active binding therefore shows up as `(function(value) ...)()`, and the function's environment is the R6 object's enclosing environment (`self`, `private`, and all their fields).
- `do.call()` puts function objects inline in the call it builds, both for `what` and for any arguments that are functions.

Both are part of how R builds these calls, so they can't be kept out of `sys.calls()`. The environments were saved with the coverage, though. In the example from the issue, `saveRDS(.counters)` segfaulted because one of them held data read with arrow.

`update_current_test()` now runs the recorded calls through `strip_function_envs()`. It walks each call (including nested calls) and gives any closure it finds an `emptyenv()` environment. Compared with the safeguard in dgkf/covr@573-record-tests-arrow-segfault:

- Calls are modified in place with `[[<-` rather than rebuilt with `as.call(lapply(...))`. Rebuilding drops the calls' `srcref` attributes, which `update_current_test()` (`has_srcref()`) and consumers of `attr(cov, "tests")` rely on.
- Elements are only reassigned if they changed, and the walk goes over `as.list()` rather than indexing into the call (which is a pairlist), so very long calls stay linear.

The `covr.record_tests` docs now say that functions in recorded calls have their environment replaced.

Fixes #573.

### Verification

- The new test records an R6 active binding and a `do.call()` with a function argument. It fails on `main` (the functions keep their environments) and passes with this change. The full suite passes with this version of covr installed.
- [dgkf/covr-r6-active-binding-test](https://github.com/dgkf/covr-r6-active-binding-test) (arrow 26.0.0, R 4.4.3), after changing `32` to `32L` in its test because `nrow()` of an arrow table is now an integer: released covr 3.6.5 segfaults in `saveRDS(.counters, ...)`. This branch completes, records both tests, and the active binding's function has `<environment: R_EmptyEnv>`.
- Overhead: `package_coverage()` of R6's source with `covr.record_tests = TRUE` took 4.4 to 5.5 s per run both with and without this change (3 runs each), so any difference is within run-to-run noise.

Other values that `do.call()` inlines into calls, such as data frames or R6 objects passed as arguments, are still recorded as they are.

title: Trace expressions in braceless branches nested in calls and function bodies
description:
Related to #279 (does not close it). This is more complete expression coverage, not branch coverage.

## Problem
covr only imputed srcrefs for the branches of `if`/`switch` when the conditional was a statement in braces. Braceless branches elsewhere shared one counter with the whole expression, so a branch that never ran was reported as covered:

```r
f <- function(x) if (x) 1 else 2      # whole body was one counter
nul <- if (FALSE)
  0L       # falsely covered
else
  1L
list(a = if (x) 1 else 2)
lapply(xs, function(i) if (x) i else -i)
(if (x) "h" else "i") -> a
paste(switch(x, a = "j", "k"))
```

## Change in reported coverage
Existing counters are kept, but new counters are added for the condition and the branch expressions of these conditionals, so **reported coverage can go down**. For example, `f <- function(x) if (x) 1 else 2` tested only with `f(TRUE)` (or only `f(FALSE)`) used to report 100% and now reports 0% by line and 75% by expression; with both it is 100%. Braceless bodies are now covered the same way as the equivalent braced code. NEWS announces this as a change in reported coverage.

## Approach
- `trace_calls()` gains an internal `impute_ref` argument: a function returning the srcref of a call that has no srcref of its own. The parse data of a call is only looked up (once, memoized for all its components) when a conditional nested in it needs a srcref; no counters are created for the call itself.
- `impute_child_srcrefs()` maps parse data onto the components of assignments (incl. `->`), infix/unary ops, parentheses, calls/subsets and `function` definitions. `impute_body_srcref()` handles braceless function bodies.
- `parse_children()` is extracted from `impute_srcref()` and now subsets the parse data frame once instead of three times.

The first version gated the lookup with `contains_conditional()`, which walked the subtree of every ancestor of a conditional (quadratic in nesting depth). It is replaced by the lazy lookup above.

## Benchmarks
R 4.4.3, Linux (WSL2, shared machine, so ~±10% noise). `main` = origin/main, `POC` = first version of this PR (with `contains_conditional()`), `PR` = this version. Each run in a fresh R process.

**knitr 1.52** (10.3k lines of pure R; installed with `--with-keep.source --with-keep.parse.data`):

| | main | POC | PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Instrumentation, `trace_environment(asNamespace("knitr"))` (median of 5, s) | 0.849 | 1.052 | 0.883 |
| Counters | 4409 | 4566 | 4566 |
| Instrumented execution, knitr's testit suite (median of 3, s) | 2.56 | 2.60 | 2.60 |

Uninstrumented, knitr's test suite takes 0.97 s.

**Synthetic nesting** (one installed package. R's parser allows ~50 levels of brackets, so depths of 50 to 200 use left-associative `+` chains, where the first term is the deepest call):
- `calls_40`: `g(g(...g(if (a) 1 else 2)...))`, 40 levels
- `chain_D`: `(if (a) 1 else 2) + 1 + ... + 1`, D levels
- `every_D`: `(if (a) 1 else 0) + ... + (if (a) 1 else 0)`, D+1 conditionals
- `braced_200`: like `every_200`, but with braced branches

Instrumentation is `trace_calls()` on one function (median of 5, then median of 3 processes). Execution is 2000 calls of the instrumented function.

| case | trace main | trace POC | trace PR | exec main | exec PR | exec uninstrumented |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| calls_40 | 0.001 | 0.032 | 0.022 | 0.016 | 0.025 | 0.012 |
| chain_50 | 0.001 | 0.030 | 0.029 | 0.005 | 0.009 | 0.001 |
| chain_100 | 0.001 | 0.073 | 0.064 | 0.005 | 0.016 | 0.001 |
| chain_200 | 0.002 | 0.205 | 0.158 | 0.006 | 0.010 | 0.002 |
| every_50 | 0.002 | 0.090 | 0.080 | 0.005 | 0.268 | 0.001 |
| every_100 | 0.003 | 0.218 | 0.156 | 0.006 | 0.626 | 0.002 |
| every_200 | 0.005 | 0.615 | 0.411 | 0.008 | 1.169 | 0.003 |
| braced_200 | 0.020 | 0.634 | 0.345 | 0.502 | 1.122 | 0.005 |

- Instrumentation on a realistic package is within noise of main (+4%). The remaining cost in the synthetic cases is one parse-data lookup per ancestor of a conditional, and each lookup scans the file's parse data. That is linear in the number of conditionals and their depth. The quadratic subtree walks are gone.
- Execution cost scales with the number of counters hit. `every_200` hits 402 more counters per call (each condition and the taken branch of 201 `if`s). That is the same cost per counter as braced code on main (`braced_200`), so it is the price of the finer coverage and not overhead in the instrumentation.

## Out of scope
Branch coverage (branch identities, implicit `else`/`switch` no-match paths, branch summaries, Cobertura branch fields) is tabled for a later release. #279 stays open for it.

## Testing
- `test-braceless.R`: percentages for a one-line braceless `if` with each outcome and with both, braced vs braceless bodies giving the same line results, and conditionals nested in an assignment, a call, named arguments, an anonymous function, a right assignment and a `switch()` inside a call.
- Full suite passes with the branch installed (`R CMD INSTALL -l $CL .; R_LIBS=$CL Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'`).

title: Add `n` argument to `print.coverage()`
description:
`print.coverage()` gains an `n = Inf` argument limiting how many files or functions are printed, as suggested in the issue thread. Rows are already sorted from least to most covered, so truncated output shows the least covered first and ends with e.g. `... and 2 more functions; use `print(x, n = Inf)` to show all`. The default `Inf` keeps the current output.

Fixes #215.

title: Report the file name for unpaired `# nocov` ranges
description:
The error for unpaired `# nocov start` / `# nocov end` comments now names the file and the lines of the comments, e.g.

```
R/TestExclusion.R has 2 range starts (lines 8, 23) but only 1 range end (line 13) for exclusion from code coverage!
```

It also no longer says "but only" when there are more ends than starts.

Fixes #409.

title: Submit git info to Coveralls from GitHub Actions
description:
`coveralls()` now adds the git commit, branch and remote to the upload when `service_name = "github-actions"` and a `repo_token` is given, so Coveralls can update the badge for the right branch.

- **Branch:** `GITHUB_HEAD_REF` (the source branch of a pull request) if it is set, otherwise `GITHUB_REF_NAME`. For pull requests `GITHUB_REF_NAME` is `<number>/merge`, so it can't be used on its own.
- **Remote:** `git config --get remote.origin.url`, which `actions/checkout` sets.
- `jenkins_git_info()` is renamed to `git_info()` and takes the branch and remote as arguments. Drone, Jenkins and travis-pro still use `CI_BRANCH` and `CI_REMOTE`.
- `?coveralls` now lists the services that submit git info.

The recommended setup on GitHub Actions is still the official `coverallsapp/github-action` with `cobertura.xml` (#664). This change makes `coveralls()` work for people who call it directly.

Fixes #535.

title: `to_sonarqube()`: write paths relative to the package root
description:
`to_sonarqube()` put the package name in front of every file path (e.g. `TestSummary/R/TestSummary.R`). SonarQube's [generic coverage format](https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/analyzing-source-code/test-coverage/generic-test-data) reads paths relative to the project's base directory. That is usually the package root, so these paths didn't match any files.

- Paths are now relative to the package root (`R/TestSummary.R`).
- New `path_prefix` argument for packages that live in a subdirectory of the SonarQube project. `path_prefix = "mypkg"` gives `mypkg/R/foo.R`, which is the same as the old output when the directory has the package's name.
- The doc link now points to the current SonarQube page.

This changes the default output, so there's a NEWS bullet that says how to get the old paths back.

Fixes #636.

title: Allow `outDir` to be passed to `package_coverage()`
description:
`package_coverage()` always passed its own `outDir` to `tools::testInstalledPackage()`, so passing `outDir` through `...` failed with `formal argument "outDir" matched by multiple actual arguments`. A user-supplied `outDir` is now used instead (created if needed), so test and example output can be kept outside `install_path`.

Fixes #518.

title: Keep `install_path` when failures are reported as warnings
description:
With `allow_failures = TRUE`, `package_coverage()` reported test failures as warnings pointing at `.Rout.fail` files, then deleted `install_path` (with the default `clean = TRUE`), so the files no longer existed. The install directory is now only removed if no failures were reported.

Failures that error already kept `install_path` (#615).

Fixes #554.

title: Include code run in forked processes in file_coverage() and friends
description:
`file_coverage()`, `code_coverage()`, `environment_coverage()`, `function_coverage()` and `with_coverage()` now include code run in processes forked by parallel's `mclapply()`, `mcparallel()` and related functions, like `package_coverage()` already does.

## How

`collect_coverage()` is a new internal helper that all five functions use. It evaluates the code and returns the coverage. While the code runs, `trace_forks()` temporarily patches the `parallel` namespace:

- `mcfork()`: the child zeroes its counters right after forking. Without this, each child's trace would also include the counts the parent had before the fork, so they would be counted twice. For example, `a(0); mclapply(1:4, a, mc.cores = 2)` would give 7 hits instead of 5.
- `mcexit()`: the child calls `save_trace()` on a temporary directory before exiting. `mclapply()` and `mccollect()` wait for the child's exit notification, which is sent after `save_trace()` runs, so the traces are complete before they are merged. The save is wrapped in `try()`: a child that outlives the call (e.g. an uncollected `mcparallel()` job) still exits cleanly.

The saved traces are merged into the session's counters with `merge_coverage()`. The original functions are restored on exit, including when the code errors.

This is on by default (except on Windows). As requested in the issue, it can be turned off the same way as for `package_coverage()`: `options(covr.fix_parallel_mcexit = FALSE)` or `COVR_FIX_PARALLEL_MCEXIT=false`. `should_enable_parallel_mcexit_fix()` now treats "no package" (in-session coverage) as enabled by default. The previously empty `covr.fix_parallel_mcexit` entry in `?covr` is now documented.

## Tests

- `test-parallel.R`: `file_coverage()` counts the `mclapply()` and `mcparallel()` hits exactly (fails before this change with `1 0` instead of `5 1`), and returns only the session's counts with the option off. Another test checks that `mcfork`/`mcexit` are restored when the code fails.
- Full suite passes (`FAIL 0 | PASS 516`) with this version of covr installed. With the CRAN covr installed, `test-full_traversal.R` fails because it needs the dev covr in `package_coverage()`'s subprocess.
- covr-on-covr via `shim_package.sh` passes, with `R/parallel.R` and `R/trace_calls.R` at 100%.

## Not changed

`package_coverage()` still counts the parent's hits from before a fork twice (a test that calls `test1()` and then `mccollect(mcparallel(...))` reports `test1` hit 2 times). This bug predates this PR, and coverage percentages are unaffected. Its `mcexit` patch is left as is.

Fixes #410.

title: Upload coverage without the organization Codecov token
description:
Fixes the test-coverage job on main, which has failed on every push since #677 (`Failed to upload coverage to codecov.io. Client error: (404) Not Found`; last success c0df663, just before #677).

The r-lib organization `CODECOV_TOKEN` isn't valid for covr's Codecov project. Codecov answers such uploads with 404 (the same symptom as #568), and since #672 `codecov()` turns that into an error. This goes back to tokenless uploads; with #672, a rate limit (429) now only warns, which was the original reason for adding the token. The action version bumps from #677 are kept.

If we want a token later, it needs to be the repository upload token from covr's Codecov settings, added as a repository secret.

title: Find partially executed compiled lines with `gcov -a`
description:
Fixes #610.

`options(covr.gcov_partial = "uncovered")` (#604) relied on the trailing `*` that gcc >= 8 adds to partially executed lines. llvm-cov (the gcov on macOS) and older gcc don't emit it, which is the macOS/Windows failure seen in #608.

covr now always runs gcov with `-a`. The extra `N-block M` lines don't match the existing line regex, so line counts are unchanged; `parse_gcov()` also reads them and treats a line as partial if it has a `*` **or** an unexecuted block.

The unexecuted block marker depends on the implementation, so `gcov_unexecuted_block()` picks it from `gcov --version`:

| gcov | non-exceptional unexecuted block | exceptional-only block |
|---|---|---|
| gcc >= 8 | `%%%%%` | `$$$$$` |
| gcc < 8 | `$$$$$` | `%%%%%` |
| llvm-cov | `$$$$$` | `$$$$$` (indistinguishable) |

(gcc swapped the markers in 8.1; see `gcov.c` in the 7.1 vs 8.1 releases.) For gcc >= 8 the block check gives the same result as `*`, so behavior on Linux is unchanged. With llvm-cov, C++ lines that only have unexecuted exception cleanup blocks (e.g. `std::string s = "abc";`) also count as partial. That's documented under `covr.gcov_partial`.

### Tests
- New `TestCompiledPartial` fixture with `if (asLogical(verbose)) Rprintf(...)`, plus an end-to-end test in `test-Compiled.R`.
- Unit tests for llvm-style output (no `*`), gcc >= 8 exceptional `$$$$$` blocks being ignored, and version detection.
- Checked by hand with clang 18 + `llvm-cov gcov`: line 5 of the fixture is reported as `0` with `"uncovered"`. Before this change it was `3`.

`test-full_traversal.R` has 3 failures locally, but those also fail on a clean `main`, so they're unrelated.

title: Test `with_coverage()` with tests that read fixtures with `test_path()`
description:
Fixes #551.

## Cause

The bug is in devtools, not covr. I reproduced it with the versions in use when the issue was filed (devtools 2.4.5, testthat 3.2.0). In that version, `test_coverage_active_file()` ran the test file from the **package root** with `TESTTHAT=true`. Under that setting `testthat::test_path("fixtures", "x.rds")` returns `fixtures/x.rds`, which doesn't exist relative to the package root. A test that failed this way was also swallowed silently, because the only active reporter was the snapshot reporter:

| test file reads the fixture… | devtools 2.4.5 | devtools 2.5.2 | `with_coverage(testthat::test_file())` (this branch) |
|---|---|---|---|
| inside `it()` | **0.00%** (the reported bug) | 100% | 100% |
| in the `describe()` body | error: cannot open `fixtures/test_data.rds` | 100% | 100% |
| in `tests/testthat/setup.R` | — | **error**: object not found | 100% |
| fixture defined inline | 100% | 100% | 100% |

devtools 2.4.6 fixed the working directory and now reports test failures (r-lib/devtools#2537). It still recreates the test runner around covr's `environment_coverage()`, which `sys.source()`s the test file. Because of that, setup files aren't run, and data loaded in `setup.R` (the issue's layout has one) still breaks `test_coverage_active_file()` with current devtools. `with_coverage()` (#655) lets devtools run `testthat::test_file()` itself, which handles all of these cases.

## Changes

- New fixture package `tests/testthat/TestFixtures`. Its tests read `fixtures/words.txt` with `test_path()` in a setup file, in a `describe()` body and in an `it()` block, and each read feeds a different function.
- New test in `test-with_coverage.R`: running `with_coverage(testthat::test_file(..., stop_on_failure = TRUE))` on that package gives 100% coverage. I checked that it fails when the fixture can't be found.
- `?environment_coverage` now explains that it only `sys.source()`s the test files from the current directory, and points testthat users to `with_coverage()` with `testthat::test_file()`.
- The `with_coverage()` NEWS bullet now mentions setup files and fixtures, and references #551.

For the setup-file case to work in devtools, `test_coverage_active_file()` needs to switch to `covr::with_coverage()`, as sketched in #655. That's a devtools change and isn't part of this PR.

## Verification

- `devtools::test()`: FAIL 0, SKIP 1, PASS 512, with this branch's covr installed. With CRAN covr 3.6.5 installed instead, `test-full_traversal.R` fails, because `package_coverage()` subprocesses load the installed covr. That failure is unrelated to this change.
- The table above comes from a reproduction package run under each setup.

title: Pass the Codecov token to covr's own coverage upload
description:
r-lib has an organization-level `CODECOV_TOKEN` secret available to covr, but `test-coverage.yaml` never passed it to `covr::codecov()`, so every upload was tokenless. Codecov rate-limits tokenless uploads, which is how #672's CI hit an HTTP 429.

- Pass `CODECOV_TOKEN` to the coverage step. covr keeps uploading with its own `codecov()` rather than `codecov-action` (as in the r-lib/actions example) so CI exercises the uploader. Pull requests from forks don't get secrets and still upload without a token; with #672, a 429/5xx there only warns.
- Update `actions/checkout` v3 → v6 and `actions/upload-artifact` v4 → v7, matching the current r-lib/actions examples.

title: Warn when a process loads the package but does not save its coverage
description:
Fixes #438.

## Problem

An R process started by the tests (a Shiny app run by shinytest/shinytest2, a callr session, a future or parallel worker) saves its coverage from a finalizer when R exits normally. If the process is killed (`SIGKILL`/`SIGTERM`) or is still running when the tests end, that coverage was dropped silently. In #438 (and the shinytest2 comments) most of the package is only run inside the app process, so coverage changed from run to run depending on whether the app was killed before it could save.

To reproduce, add a test that runs package code in `callr::r_bg()` and then calls `$kill()`. That code shows as uncovered and there is no warning. Stopping it with `$interrupt(); $wait()` instead counts the coverage.

## Change

- The loader hook now calls `covr:::register_trace(ns, dir)`. It creates a `covr_pending_<pid>_*` marker next to the trace files and registers the finalizer, which saves the trace and then removes the marker. Only the process that created the marker removes it, so forked (`mcparallel`) children don't remove their parent's marker.
- After running the tests, `package_coverage()` gives a warning of class `covr_unsaved_trace` if other processes left markers behind, e.g.:
  ```
  1 R process loaded KillTest but did not save its coverage, so it is missing from the results.
  Coverage is saved when R exits normally; it is lost if a process is killed (e.g. with SIGKILL or SIGTERM) or is still running when the tests finish.
  Stop background processes started by the tests, such as Shiny apps, callr sessions or future workers, gracefully and wait for them to exit.
  ```
  Markers left by the main process are ignored, since it can load the instrumented package itself (e.g. for `\Sexpr`).
- Added a section on coverage in subprocesses to `?package_coverage`, including shinytest2's `AppDriver$stop()`, which already waits longer under covr. Also updated the "How it works" vignette and NEWS.

Since the hook now calls a new `covr:::` function, the processes started by `package_coverage()` need this covr to be installed. That is already how `R CMD check` and the test-coverage workflow run. Running `devtools::test()` with an older covr installed now fails the `package_coverage()` tests, so I added a note to AGENTS.md.

## Testing

- New test: one `code` subprocess exits normally and another kills itself with `SIGKILL`. The test snapshots the warning, which should report one process, checks that the function run by the normal process is covered, and checks that the function run by the killed process is not. It fails on `main`.
- `devtools::test()` with this covr installed: 478 pass, 0 warnings. None of the existing `package_coverage()` tests give a false warning (vignettes, examples, `mcparallel` in `TestParallel`).
- `R CMD check`: 0 errors. The only warning and notes come from my machine (`qpdf`, `.git` in the worktree, timestamps).
- Ran the `callr::r_bg()` reproduction by hand: `$kill()` now gives the warning, and a graceful stop gives full coverage and no warning.

title: Don't report `# nocov` lines of partially excluded expressions
description:
An expression is only dropped by `exclude()` if all of its lines are excluded, so the `# nocov` first and last lines of a function defined inside another function were still reported as uncovered. `exclude()` now records the excluded lines on the coverage object, and `tally_coverage()` and `per_line()` (used by `report()`, `codecov()` and `coveralls()`) leave them out.

Fixes #594.

title: Error in `codecov()` when the upload fails
description:
`codecov()` now checks the HTTP status of the upload response and throws an error including the status and the body returned by codecov.io, so CI jobs fail instead of silently succeeding.

Fixes #565.

title: Add `to_lcov()` to write LCOV tracefiles
description:
New `to_lcov()` writes a coverage object as an LCOV tracefile ([geninfo(1)](https://manpages.debian.org/unstable/lcov/geninfo.1.en.html) format), modeled on `to_cobertura()` and `to_sonarqube()`.

For each source file it writes:

- `FN`/`FNDA`/`FNF`/`FNH` from `tally_coverage(by = "function")`. The function line is its first traced line, and its count is the largest count of any of its expressions.
- `DA`/`LF`/`LH` from `tally_coverage(by = "line")`, the same line counts used by `report()` and `percent_coverage()`.

Branch coverage is not recorded. `SF` paths are written as covr reports them, which for a package means relative to the package root. Counts are formatted with `%.0f` so large counts don't come out as `1e+05`.

Example output for `tests/testthat/TestSummary`:

```
TN:
SF:R/TestSummary.R
FN:5,test_me
FN:13,dont_test_me
FNDA:1,test_me
FNDA:0,dont_test_me
FNF:2
FNH:1
DA:5,1
DA:6,1
DA:8,0
DA:13,0
LF:4
LH:2
end_of_record
```

Verification:
- lcov 2.0's `lcov --summary` and `genhtml`, run from the package root, both read this file: 2 of 4 lines and 1 of 2 functions covered.
- Tried it on `TestCompiled`. gcov files get `DA` records and `FNF:0`, because compiled code has no function names.
- `devtools::test()`: the new tests pass. The only failures are the 3 in `test-full_traversal.R`, which also fail on `main` in this environment.

Fixes #442.

title: Handle empty files in R/ when splitting on line directives
description:
Fixes #522.

## Cause
R CMD INSTALL concatenates the files in `R/` and puts a `#line 1 "file"` directive before each one. For an empty file, `split_on_line_directives()` computed `end == start - 1`, so `lines[start:end]` returned a reversed two-element range instead of nothing:

- an empty file in the middle got the next file's directive plus its own
- an empty **last** file got `c(NA, <its own directive>)`

In covr 3.6.5, `getParseData(..., includeText = TRUE)` errors on that `NA` (`invalid 'length.out' value`), so tracing failed and `package_coverage()` reported 0% coverage. That's why renaming `collapse.R` to `z_collapse.R` worked around it: the empty file was no longer last. Since #644 (`includeText = NA`), the dev version no longer errors, but the split was still wrong.

## Fix
Empty files now get `character()`.

## Verification
- New test in `test-utils.R` covering empty first, middle and last files.
- Reproduced with a package containing `R/a.R` (code) and an empty `R/d.R`: covr 3.6.5 returned `NULL` coverage. With this branch installed, a package with empty first, middle and last files reports the expected 75%. The split output also parses with `includeText = TRUE`.
- `devtools::test()`: all pass, except `test-full_traversal.R`, which fails locally only because its subprocess picks up the user-library covr 3.6.5. It passes with this branch installed.

title: Credit #642 in the NEWS bullet for character-based failure messages
description:
The byte/character mismatch in `show_failures()` reported in #642 was fixed by #654, which bounds the failure message using `nchar(type = "chars")` throughout and adds a multibyte regression test (`covr_error keeps full output and a bounded message`). This adds the issue to the NEWS bullet.

Fixes #642.

title: Add `coverage_to_markdown()`
description:
Formats coverage as a markdown table, optionally compared against a baseline coverage object.

Fixes #519.

title: Handle switch() called with the base pipe
description:
Fixes #630.

For `x |> switch(a = , b = 1)`, `impute_srcref()` matched the srcref of the whole pipe expression, so its "children" were `lhs PIPE rhs` rather than the switch's arguments. The imputed srcrefs were misaligned, and a fall-through case (`a = ,`) was traced as if it had a value, so evaluating it gave `argument is missing, with no default`.

Now, when the expression is a pipe, covr uses the parse data of the right-hand call with the left-hand side inserted as its first argument, so a piped switch is handled exactly like `switch(x, ...)`.

- Regression test in test-braceless.R (piped version of the existing drop-through test): fails on main, passes with the fix; full suite passes.
- The reprex from the issue errors with covr main and with the fix gives the same coverage as the unpiped form (subject 3, `*` body 3, `stop()` 0).

title: Add example `.covrignore` to README
description:
Adds an example `.covrignore` to the README and clarifies that paths are relative to the package root and refer to source files, not tests.

Fixes #350.

title: Add with_coverage() for running code such as test files under coverage
description:
Proof of concept for #543 (related to #543, not intended to close it yet).

## API

```r
with_coverage(code, env = parent.frame(), line_exclusions = NULL, function_exclusions = NULL)
```

Same shape as `environment_coverage()`, but `code` is an arbitrary expression instead of a vector of files to `sys.source()`. It is a lazy promise evaluated in the caller's frame after `env` has been instrumented, inside `R_COVR=true`. Returns a `coverage` object; traces are reset and counters cleared with `on.exit()` (so also on error). I picked this over a `test_file`-specific function / extra argument on `environment_coverage()` because it is the smallest thing that covers `test_file()`, `test_dir()`, `test_local()`, `source()`, or any other runner, and does not make covr depend on testthat.

```r
pkgload::load_all("path/to/pkg", export_all = TRUE)
cov <- covr::with_coverage(
  testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-foo.R", package = "pkg", reporter = "silent"),
  env = asNamespace("pkg")
)
```

## The chicken-and-egg problem

It turns out not to be one: `trace_environment()` does not replace bindings in `env`, it rewrites each function object **in place** (`covr_reassign_function` swaps body/formals/attributes of the existing closure). So any reference to those functions, including those reached from the child-of-the-namespace environment `test_file()` creates for the tests, runs the instrumented body. `code` only has to avoid *re-creating* the functions after tracing.

## Limitations

- `testthat::test_file(load_package = "source")` runs `pkgload::load_all()` itself, which replaces the traced functions with fresh ones, so coverage is silently 0% (verified: 0.00%). The default `load_package = "none"` (with `package = "pkg"`) is the one to use; documented in `?with_coverage`.
- The caller must load the package (e.g. `load_all()`) and pass the namespace as `env`; `with_coverage()` does not do it. Source references are required (`load_all()` keeps them).
- Not cheap-to-fix but not needed: no per-file filtering (devtools still does that itself), no reporting.
- `pkgload` added to Suggests (tests only).

## Verified

- Tests in `tests/testthat/test-with_coverage.R`: plain env, lazy eval in the caller, `R_COVR`, exclusions, cleanup on success/error, and `test_file()` on load_all()ed fixtures `TestSummary`, `TestS4`, `TestR6` giving data frames identical (file, function, lines, counts) to `package_coverage()` on the same fixture, plus a failing test file (`TestFailure`, `stop_on_failure = TRUE`) leaves functions/counters restored.
- `devtools::test()`: FAIL 0 / SKIP 2 / PASS 448.

## How `devtools::test_coverage_active_file()` could use it

The reporter/snapshotter/`local_test_directory()` setup collapses to testthat's own runner:

```r
env <- load_all(pkg$path, quiet = TRUE, export_all = export_all)$env
coverage <- covr::with_coverage(
  testthat::test_file(test_file, package = pkg$package, reporter = "stop"?? / default),
  env = env,
  ...
)
# then the existing filter / relative / report code
```

(`test_file()` handles `local_test_directory`, snapshot start/end and the stop-on-failure behaviour; devtools would pass `stop_on_failure = TRUE` and a progress reporter.) I did not touch devtools.

title: Fix main CI: R >= 4.6 compilation and covr-on-covr full traversal test
description:
`main` has been failing CI since #666:

1. **Compilation on R >= 4.6.** `covr_is_unforced_promise()` used `findVarInFrame3()` and `PRVALUE()`, which are no longer exposed in R 4.6's headers. On R >= 4.6 it now uses `R_GetBindingType(sym, env) == R_BindingTypeDelayed`; older R keeps the existing code.
2. **test-coverage job.** "full traversal is enabled from DESCRIPTION" failed when measuring covr's own coverage: `read_description()` lowercases field names, so after `shim_package.sh` renamed covr to covrShim the lookup key `config/covrShim/full_traversal` no longer matched. The key is now lowercased at lookup, and the shim scripts also rename in fixture DESCRIPTION files (the only one mentioning covr is TestFullTraversal's `Config/covr/full_traversal`).

Checked locally: builds without warnings on R 4.3.3, 4.4.3 and 4.6.2; `test-full_traversal.R` passes on all three; `is_unforced_promise()` gives identical results on 4.3.3 and 4.6.2 (unforced promise TRUE without forcing it, plain value FALSE, forced promise FALSE); the shimmed covr-on-covr run with `CI=true` fails on the old code (FAIL 3) and passes with the fix; shim/unshim round-trips cleanly.

title: Re-document with roxygen2 8.1.1
description:
Contributors (and agents) were documenting with a mix of roxygen2 7.3.3 and 8.1.1, so unrelated `man/`, `NAMESPACE` and `DESCRIPTION` changes kept showing up in PRs. This re-documents with the current CRAN release, roxygen2 8.1.1:

- `DESCRIPTION`: `RoxygenNote: 7.3.3` is replaced by `Config/roxygen2/version: 8.1.1`.
- `NAMESPACE`: `importFrom()` directives are grouped by package (roxygen2 8 format).
- `man/new_counter.Rd`: corrected link target for `base::srcref()`.

No code changes. Installs and loads on R 4.3.3. CI will fail on R >= 4.6 until #669 is merged (main is currently broken there).

title: Optionally trace functions nested in lists and environments
description:
Functions stored inside lists and environments, such as `fns <- list(a = function(x) x)`, functions defined inside `local()`, and ggproto methods, were never traced. covr only traced top-level functions plus S4, RC, R6, S7 and box methods.

Full traversal is **off by default**, because walking every object can be slow for packages with large data. Enable it with:

- `Config/covr/full_traversal: true` in a package's DESCRIPTION, or
- `options(covr.full_traversal = TRUE)`, which takes precedence when set.

`package_coverage()` passes the setting to the child process through `add_hooks()`, the same way as `covr.record_tests`.

The traversal (`R/traverse.R`):

- never walks namespaces (so the lazydata environment is never touched), attached packages, or the global, base and empty environments
- only traces functions whose enclosing environments lead to the traced environment, not to another package's namespace
- tracks objects by address (new `covr_address()` C helper), so cycles and shared lists are walked once, separately created closures are each traced, and functions already handled by the S4/RC/R6/S7/box code are skipped
- skips unevaluated promises (new `covr_is_unforced_promise()` C helper), so delayed arguments aren't evaluated early
- reads list elements with `.subset2()`, so class methods such as `[[.numeric_version` are not called
- walks breadth first and names every copy of a function after the first one found, so methods get names like `GeomRect$draw_panel`

On ggplot2 4.0.3, full traversal traces 10,352 expressions (5,924 without it). Run time goes from about 100s to 112s, and existing counts are unchanged.

Fixes #113.

title: Document uploading to Coveralls from GitHub Actions
description:
Use the official `coverallsapp/github-action` with the `cobertura.xml` file the standard `test-coverage` workflow already creates, instead of `covr::coveralls()`. No Coveralls token is needed.

Fixes #457.

title: Update bundled Bootstrap to 3.4.1
description:
`report()` and `file_report()` bundled Bootstrap 3.3.5, which security scanners flag for known XSS vulnerabilities (e.g. CVE-2018-14040/14041/14042, CVE-2019-8331).

- Updated the vendored `bootstrap.min.css`, `bootstrap-theme.min.css`, and `bootstrap.min.js` in `inst/www/shared/bootstrap` to 3.4.1 from the official npm release (source-map comments stripped because the `.map` files aren't shipped). It's the same major version, so the report markup is unchanged.
- Bumped the version in `html_dependency_bootstrap()`.
- Removed the unused `tests/testthat/test-report.htm` fixture (it referenced Bootstrap 3.3.7 and was only used by a commented-out test) and replaced that commented-out test with one checking that `report()` writes the 3.4.1 assets.

Verified by generating a report for `TestS4` in a browser: Bootstrap reports version 3.4.1, and clicking a file in the table switches to the Source tab as before.

Note: Bootstrap 3 is end-of-life, and some scanners also flag 3.4.1 for CVE-2024-6484 (carousel component, which covr doesn't use). Moving to Bootstrap 5 would need markup changes and is out of scope here.

Fixes #639.

title: Document the coverage object and fix `value()`
description:
Fixes #564.

* `?package_coverage` now has a **Value** section describing the returned `coverage` object: one element per traced R expression / compiled line with `value`, `srcref`, `functions` (and `tests` with `covr.record_tests`), what the element names like `assign.c:122:1:122:367:1:367:122:122` mean, the `package`/`root`/`library` attributes, the `coverages` list returned with `combine_types = FALSE`, and which helpers to use to get a data frame, percentages, or uncovered lines.
* `function_coverage()`, `file_coverage()`, `code_coverage()` and `environment_coverage()` link to that section.
* New `?as.data.frame.coverage` topic documents each column (`first_byte` vs `first_column`, `first_parsed`, the `sort` argument, etc.). `?tally_coverage` documents its line-level columns, including that a line's `value` is the minimum over its expressions, and now has examples.
* `value()` previously errored on any coverage of R code (`no applicable method for 'value' applied to an object of class "list"`), because only compiled-code elements have a class. It now returns a named numeric vector of execution counts for any coverage object. The methods for the `expression_coverage(s)` classes, which are never created, are replaced by a default method.

Roxygen was run with 8.1.1 locally; unrelated churn it produced (`RoxygenNote`, `NAMESPACE` formatting, `covr-package.Rd`, `new_counter.Rd`) was not committed.

Tests: new `tests/testthat/test-value.R` (fails on main, passes here); full `devtools::test()` passes (465 pass, 2 skip). Checked `value()` on `TestCompiled` coverage covering both R and C/C++ elements, ran the new examples, and `pkgdown::check_pkgdown()` reports no problems.

title: Keep report tabs visible and remember scroll position
description:
- The Files / Source tabs in `report()` are now sticky, so they stay at the top of the page while scrolling.
- Each tab remembers its scroll position, so returning to the file list after viewing a file puts you back where you were. Opening a new file starts at the top of its source.
- File links no longer follow `href="#"`, which jumped to the top of the page and added `#` to the URL.

Fixes #232.

title: Document that `skip_on_cran()` tests are skipped during coverage
description:
Add a README FAQ entry explaining `NOT_CRAN`.

Fixes #521.

title: Count partially executed gcov lines
description:
Fixes #604.

gcov marks lines where only some blocks ran with a trailing `*`, e.g. `3*:    4:  if (verbose) printf(...)` when `verbose` is always false. `parse_gcov()`'s pattern didn't allow `*`, so these lines were dropped entirely: counted as neither covered nor uncovered.

- By default they now count as covered, with gcov's execution count.
- `options(covr.gcov_partial = "uncovered")` counts them as 0, so CI can require every part of a line to run (the strict mode asked for in the issue). Documented in `?covr`.

Verified on a small package whose C function has `if (asLogical(v)) Rprintf(...)` and is only called with `FALSE`: line 5 is missing on main, `5=1` by default and `5=0` with the option. New unit test fails on main (FAIL 2) and passes with the fix; full suite passes.

title: Keep full failure output in covr errors
description:
Fixes #570.

`covr_error` now carries `file` and `output` (full failure output); `print()` shows the last `n` lines (default 50). The message stays bounded by `warning.length` (characters, not bytes), and the header-skip bug is fixed. `covr_warning` from `allow_failures` carries the same fields.

title: Add missing NEWS bullet for covr 3.6.2
description: Fixes #534. The 3.6.2 CRAN release fixed S3 generic/method signature consistency (4853eaa) and skipped an R6 test on R-devel (2b9b4dd), but its NEWS section was empty.

title: README: should I add covr to Suggests?
description: Fixes #515. Adds a FAQ entry based on the answer in the issue: not required, but useful (local installs via devtools/pak, tracking usage); `usethis::use_coverage()` adds it.

title: Print a message when the RStudio addin starts
description: Fixes #404. `addin_report()` now prints `Calculating test coverage for <path>...` before calling `package_coverage()`, which is quiet by default and can take a while.

title: Handle switch() with a trailing comma
description:
Fixes #483.

A trailing comma in `switch()` adds an empty final argument that has no `expr` in the parse data, so `impute_srcref()` returned one fewer srcref than the call has arguments and `Map()` warned "longer argument not a multiple of length of shorter" (an error under `options(warn = 2)`). The srcref list is now padded to the length of the call; the empty argument gets no srcref and is left untraced.

Regression test in test-braceless.R fails before / passes after.

title: Add .git-blame-ignore-revs for the air reformat
description: GitHub uses this file automatically; locally run `git config blame.ignoreRevsFile .git-blame-ignore-revs`.

title: Write trace files atomically and report failed saves
description:
Fixes #509.

- `save_trace()` writes to `.covr_tmp_*` then `file.rename()`s to `covr_trace_*`; leftovers are ignored by the existing pattern.
- On `saveRDS()` failure (e.g. ALTREP), an error marker (message + pid) is written instead.
- `merge_coverage()` raises `covr_error` naming the file for corrupt files and markers; with `allow_failures = TRUE` it becomes a `covr_warning` and the file is skipped.

title: Add AGENTS.md
description:
Initial AGENTS.md based on the tidy template (`use_tidy_agents()`, as in usethis/purrr/rlang/cli/pkgdown), adapted for covr:

- **This package** section: what covr does, R >= 3.1 compatibility (no `|>` / `\()`), calling optional deps via `pkg::fun()` rather than importing (#623), fixture line numbers, `load_all()` vs install for namespace-loading checks, and the release / pkgdown steps (see #626).
- Code style drops the base pipe and `\()` rules.
- NEWS rules follow covr's existing convention (wrapped bullets, newest first) instead of unwrapped/alphabetical.

The air instructions reference `air.toml`, added in #649; merge that first.

title: Format code with air
description:
Adds an `air.toml` and does a one-time reformat of the package with [air](https://posit-dev.github.io/air/). No behavior changes.

Two commits: `Add air.toml` (config + `.Rbuildignore`) and `Reformat with air` (formatter output only, plus one `# fmt: skip`).

## Excluded from formatting
Coverage tests assert exact line numbers/expressions inside these fixtures, so they must stay byte-for-byte unchanged:
- `tests/testthat/Test*/` (fixture packages)
- `tests/testthat/a/`, `tests/testthat/b/`
- `tests/testthat/corner-cases.R`, `tests/testthat/corner-cases-test.R`

One in-test fixture in `test-covr.R` ("duplicated first_line") relies on a single-line `lapply(1:2, function(x) { x + 1 })`, so that line is marked `# fmt: skip`. Without it the test failed (`first_lines[1]` 65 vs `first_lines[2]` 66).

## Testing
- `devtools::test()`: FAIL 0, WARN 0, SKIP 2, PASS 429
- `devtools::document()`: no changes to `man/`
- `air format --check .` passes

## Follow-up
After squash-merge, add the merge commit SHA to `.git-blame-ignore-revs` in a follow-up.

title: Add option to report coverage despite test failures
description:
Closes #533

Adds `allow_failures` to `package_coverage()`, defaulting to `getOption("covr.allow_failures", FALSE)`, so the default behavior is unchanged.

When enabled, failures in tests, vignettes, examples, or `code` are collected and re-signaled as warnings (class `covr_warning`) after all steps have run. Coverage is then computed and returned as usual, so `options(covr.allow_failures = TRUE); covr::report()` works after a failed test run. The docs note that coverage may be incomplete because code after a failure is not tracked.

Implementation: `show_failures()` now signals its `covr_error` inside a `covr_continue` restart. `package_coverage()` installs a `covr_error` calling handler that records the error and invokes the restart only when `allow_failures` is `TRUE`. Otherwise the error propagates as before. Warnings are emitted outside the existing `quiet` handler so they are not muffled.

Tests: new `TestFailure` fixture package (one passing and one failing test). The tests check that the default raises `covr_error`, and that with the option set the call returns coverage (`covered` > 0, `not_covered` == 0) along with a `covr_warning`. Full suite: 425 pass, 0 fail.
